topic.title: Introduction to GacUI
topic.p:
GacUI is a high performance cross-platform C++ UI library with built-in
rich control libraries
powerful layout mechanism
control/item template mechanism
reactive design
object/list/tree data binding
MVVM support

GacUI XML Resource is an recommended to build a GacUI application. The provided toolchain consumes GacUI XML Resource and output:
A compiled binary resource format.
Such binary files contain only resources like text, image, rich text documents, etc.
Per-platform compiled Workflow assemblies. (unrecommended)
These assemblies are compiled from XML descripted UIs, animations, localed texts, etc.
You need to know what CPU platform the application is running one to load the correct assembly file at runtime. Reflection must be enabled in order to execute the assembly.
C++20 files translated from above assemblies. (recommended)
These C++ files are compiled from XML descripted UIs, animations, located texts, etc.
If all UI objects are known and no code need to be dynamically downloaded, instead of loading assemblies with reflection enabled at runtime, you can link all generated C++ code with your application to avoid enabling Reflection.
In this way your application could start very quickly and reduce 90% of the binary size.

topic.title: Supported Platforms
topic.p: These platforms are supported at this moment:

ul.li:
Linux with Wayland: Finished but you have to built toolchain by yourself. (https://github.com/vczh-libraries/wGac)
vl::presentation::elements::wgac::SetupWGacRenderer();

macOS: Almost all features are working, hosted mode is under development. (https://github.com/vczh-libraries/iGac)
SetupOSXCoreGraphicsRenderer();

topic.title: Hosted Mode
Terminal applications
topic.p: GacUI can render a local text user interface using the supplied TuiSkin and SetupTuiWindowsRenderer() on Windows, vl::presentation::wayland::SetupTuiWaylandRenderer() on Linux, or vl::presentation::osx::SetupTuiCocoaRenderer() on macOS. Windows, popups and dialogs share the terminal viewport; layout coordinates count terminal cells. Start with Build a terminal application for console startup, resource packaging and supported controls.

topic.title: Remote Protocols (core and renderer)
topic.p: The remote protocol separates a GacUI application into a headless core and a renderer. Native renderers are available on Windows, Linux and macOS. GacJS supplies an HTML5 renderer; its primary feature is running the core in the browser as WebAssembly, with working demos available.

GacUI offers a JSON remote protocol channel on top of vl::inter_process. The application chooses the underlying data-transmission implementation, such as the cross-platform async-TCP Mini HTTP transport, the Windows named-pipe transport, or the Windows HTTP.sys/WinHTTP transport from VlppOS, and the channel layer translates between that transport and the strongly typed remote protocol.

The INetworkProtocol and IChannel interface families are provided only for test-purpose local cross-process communication. Its public contracts can be reused directly, but product code is strongly recommended to provide its own implementation while keeping the GacUI JSON channel layer unchanged.

topic.title: Remote Protocols (with custom transports)
topic.p: Current examples of the JSON remote protocol channel using vl::inter_process.
The test applications exercise Windows named pipe (/Pipe), Windows HTTP.sys/WinHTTP (/Http) and portable Mini HTTP over loopback TCP (/MiniHttp): Core and Renderer.

topic.title: GacJS: WebAssembly and HTML5
topic.p: WebAssembly is the primary feature and purpose of GacJS. It builds on HTML5 rendering and the remote protocol: the browser loads the GacUI core from a .wasm file in a worker, then exposed functions and callbacks carry channel messages between JavaScript and the core. The HTML5 renderer uses the remote protocol channel, and a TypeScript view model can use Workflow RPC channels over the same WebAssembly transport.

WebAssembly and HTTP are alternative transports, independent of HTML5 rendering and view-model implementation. The HTTP option connects to a native core on Windows, Linux or macOS and is used mainly to test HTML5 rendering without WebAssembly.

Working demos in GacUI's Test/Linux are WasmFCT (FullControlTest), WasmRPT (RemoteProtocolTest) and WasmRVMT (RemoteViewModelTest). Their GacJS pages are /wasm-fct/, /wasm-rpt/ and /wasm-rvmt/; the last runs its TypeScript view model in the page. See GacJS Network Protocol for the transport contract and GacJS Projects for building and serving the demos.
